elements.content: Communication Goal: I can talk about hobbies, express preferences, and use object pronouns.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 5. Free time
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Perfect hobby
- Materials: Hobby cards, preference chart, survey sheet, COSYmanuals 'like/love/hate' and 'adverbs of frequency' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• talk about hobbies
• use like/love/hate + -ing
• use object pronouns to avoid repetition

Prior learning: Recycles present simple and frequency adverbs.

Core Active Vocabulary (15 items):

reading — looking at and understanding text. Example: Reading is my favourite hobby.
cooking — making food. Example: He loves cooking.
painting — making pictures with paint. Example: She enjoys painting.
dancing — moving your body to music. Example: They like dancing.
music — sounds made with voices or instruments. Example: We listen to music together.
cinema — a place to watch films. Example: We go to the cinema on Friday.
hobby — an activity you enjoy in free time. Example: My hobby is reading.
sport — a physical game or activity. Example: Football is a popular sport.
game — an activity with rules. Example: We play a game after class.
enjoy — to like doing something. Example: I enjoy swimming.
them — the object pronoun for plural things. Example: I love films. I love them.
him — the object pronoun for a man. Example: I know him.
her — belonging to a woman or girl. Example: Her bag is red.
it — a thing or animal. Example: It is a big city.
prefer — to like one thing more. Example: I prefer tea.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• My hobby is reading. (naming a hobby)
• I like reading. / I love dancing. (expressing preference)
• I hate cooking. (expressing dislike)
• I like them. / I don't like it. (using object pronouns)
• My brother loves music. I love it too. (agreeing with an object pronoun)
• How often do you...? (asking about frequency)

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use 'like', 'love', 'enjoy', and 'hate' to talk about preferences.

Form:
Like / love / hate + -ing: Subject + like / love / enjoy / hate + verb-ing. I like reading. She loves dancing. They hate cooking.

Examples:
• I like reading.
• She loves dancing.
• We enjoy playing football.
• He hates cooking.
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
I like ___. (read)
She loves ___. (dance)
They hate ___. (cook)
We enjoy ___. (play) football.
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I like ... (-ing).
• I love ... (-ing).
• I hate ... (-ing).
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What do you like doing in your free time?
• What do you hate doing?
• What does your friend love doing?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your hobbies with 'like/love/hate + -ing'.
• Write three sentences about a friend's hobbies.
Reading: Perfect hobby

My perfect hobby is reading. I read every evening. I like it because it is relaxing. My sister loves dancing and painting. She does them every weekend. My brother likes cooking, but he hates washing the dishes. He doesn't like it. My friend goes to the cinema every weekend. She loves films, and I love them too. What is your perfect hobby? How often do you do it?
What is the writer's hobby?
What does the brother hate?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What's your hobby?
B: I love painting. I paint every weekend.
A: Do you like music?
B: Yes, I enjoy listening to music while I paint.
A: What about sport?
B: I don't like sport, but I sometimes play games with my friends. I like them because they are fun.
What is the speaker's hobby?
Why does the speaker like games?
Speaking task: Compare your hobbies and preferences. Use object pronouns when you agree or disagree.

• What is your hobby?
• What do you love doing?
• What do you hate doing?
• Do you like films? Why?
• How often do you do your hobby?
Role-play: You are at a hobby club fair. Ask three people about their hobbies and say what you think of them.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about your hobbies using like/love/hate + -ing and object pronouns.
Model: I like ... I love ... I hate ... I like them because ...
